strategy.summary: Reproduce scipy/special hyp1f1 complex-z wrong value at buggy commit dc9cbc03c039 (PR 20805, 2024-05-27). Build SciPy from source at that commit with era-pinned numpy 1.26.4, Cython 3.0.10, and the reporter's pythran 0.15.0 and pybind11 2.12.0 (the last two are unbounded in the evidence; I chose the reporter's versions and say so). Apply the PR test diff to test_hypergeometric.py and run only test_complex_z. On buggy, hyp1f1(-0.25,0.5,1+2j) returns (1+0j), so the assert_allclose with rtol=4e-15 fails. On fixed, that case matches the reference and passes; the two xfail-marked cases may XPASS, which is not a failure.

build_commands: git checkout dc9cbc03c039 && git submodule update --init --recursive
pip install numpy==1.26.4 cython==3.0.10 pythran==0.15.0 pybind11==2.12.0 meson-python ninja pytest mpmath
git apply the PR test diff for scipy/special/tests/test_hypergeometric.py and test_specfun.py onto the buggy checkout
pinned_because: numpy 1.26.4: era ceiling (<=1.26, newest at PR date) and the reporter's version; numerically relevant, era-inferred, not a documented constraint
scipy source at dc9cbc03c039: the defect lives in scipy/special/special/specfun/specfun.h cchg(), so the build must be from this commit (also era-inferred, reporter reported 1.13.1)
cython 3.0.10: era ceiling <=3.0 per evidence; not numerically relevant, chosen to match reporter
pythran 0.15.0 and pybind11 2.12.0: unbounded in the evidence (no documented constraint, no era entry); chosen to match reporter's build deps, not required by any documented rule

strategy.success_criterion: Buggy revision: the parametrized case (-0.25, 0.5, 1+2j) with ref 1.1814553180903435-1.2792130661292984j fails at assert_allclose(rtol=4e-15) because hyp1f1 returns (1+0j). Fixed revision (PR head with the restored cchg line): that case passes, and the two pytest.param xfail cases may XPASS (non-strict xfail, not a failure). The transition is FAIL on buggy and PASS on fixed for the (-0.25,0.5,1+2j) case.
risks: Platform/toolchain: the evidence does not show the defect is architecture- or sanitizer-specific, but it was observed with the reporter's gcc 13.2.1 and MKL 2023.2 build. The cchg path is pure C++ specfun, so BLAS/LAPACK backend is probably irrelevant, but this is inferred, not stated; openblas configuration is listed as unknown.

Tolerance: rtol=4e-15 is very tight. Last-digit differences from compiler flags, FMA contraction, or libm can flip a pass to a fail on the fixed revision. Compare with the reference values before concluding.

Non-xfail cases beyond the defect case: (25,1.5,-2j) and (12,-1.5,-10+20j) are not xfail-marked. The PR says hyp1f1 can still be very inaccurate, so these may fail even on the fixed revision. The success criterion relies on the (-0.25,0.5,1+2j) case only.

Reference conflict: the issue patch expects 1.1814553180903438-1.2792130661292982j, while the test expects ...435-...984j. The difference is about 3e-16 relative, inside rtol 4e-15, so either passes, but the exact reference is not settled by the evidence.
Removed test: test_cchg_branches (0.1, 1, 7-24j) with the old value is suspect per the Matlab check; do not use it as a reference. The test_specfun.py deletion does not affect the transition.
Class name of the test is not given in the diff hunk; the -k selector avoids needing it.
Build time: scipy from source with pythran is slow; ccache helps on rebuilds. Both buggy and fixed builds are required.

oracle.reference_source: mpmath.hyp1f1, verified against Wolfram Alpha (per PR test comments); issue reference for the defect case from SciPy 1.8.0 and Wolfram Alpha
oracle.why: Complex-z hyp1f1 values are compared against high-precision references; the defect returns a wrong value (1+0j), far outside tolerance.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy commit, hyp1f1(-0.25,0.5,1+2j) returns (1+0j) because the line dropped from cchg() in specfun.h is missing. assert_allclose(h, 1.18145...-1.27921...j, rtol=4e-15) fails, since the result differs by far more than the tolerance.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed commit with the restored cchg line, hyp1f1(-0.25,0.5,1+2j) returns a value within rtol 4e-15 of the reference, so the (-0.25,0.5,1+2j) parametrized case passes. The xfail cases may XPASS, which does not fail the run.
